title: Streaming handshake fallback and machine-readable retry-hint encoding for OpenAI-compat
author: Camila Ortega
description:
Motivation: Streaming clients (especially multiplexed tool/function channels) have intermittent breakage when a downstream pod applies backpressure or when transient rate-limits are signaled mid-stream. Existing OpenAI-compat behavior returns ambiguous 429s or closes streams without a machine-readable advisory, which causes client-side retries to be either too aggressive or unsafe for tool-calls. This PR introduces a streaming handshake + graceful fallback path and a compact machine-readable retry-hint encoding to reduce failed work and make idempotency TTLs explicit for in-flight tool invocations.

Design summary: The change is three-fold: 1) Streaming handshake: on stream start we include an optional Negotiation frame that contains server-supported features (max-multiplexed-streams, max-idempotency-ttl-seconds, supports-retry-advice). Clients can opt into the handshake; the runtime will respond with a negotiated subset. If the handshake fails or is not understood, the server falls back to a conservative default so older clients continue to operate. 2) Retry-hint encoding: a compact HTTP header X-Redwood-Retry that carries a base64-encoded, signed advice bundle (proto v1) with fields: backoff_ms, retry_scope (channel/actor/request), transient:bool, advice_id. This makes retry decisions machine-readable for SDKs while remaining opaque enough to evolve. 3) Idempotency TTL refresh: when a tool/function call is streamed and the server issues a retry-hint that includes a TTL extension, the runtime will either extend the idempotency session TTL (if supported by backend) or emit a short-lived lease token that clients can present on replay to avoid double-execution.

Changes in this PR: - protocol definitions: internal/protocol/retry_hint.proto (v1) and a minimal codec in internal/protocol/codec.go. - OpenAI compat: src/openai/compat/streaming_handshake.go adds handshake frame parsing and conservative fallback. - Runtime: pkg/runtime/streaming/negotiation.go implements negotiation policy and TTL extension hooks. - Idempotency: pkg/idempotency/lease_manager.go implements short-lived lease tokens and server-side TTL extension API. - SDK adapters: redwood-sdk-python/compat/handshake.py and redwood-sdk-typescript/compat/handshake.ts include client-side helpers to surface retry-hints and lease tokens to app code. - Docs: docs/openai/compat/retry-guidance.md with suggested client behavior and examples. - Tests: unit and integration tests for handshake, encoding, and lease flows added under test/streaming.

Compatibility and rollout: Defaults are conservative. If a client does not send the handshake, the server behaves like today (no new errors, only better hints when possible). The X-Redwood-Retry header is optional and opaque; SDKs will attempt to decode but fall back to existing heuristics on failure. We will gate TTL-extension on a new runtime feature flag (off by default) and enable it incrementally for internal customers in Dedicated before a wider rollout.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for proto encoder/decoder and codec edge cases. - E2E stream tests introduced that simulate mid-stream 429/backpressure and assert that the client receives a retry-hint and that idempotency lease tokens are issued when configured. - Load test harness in benchmark-lab simulates multiplexed channels to validate handshake overhead <0.12ms per stream start under typical loads.

Risk and mitigations: - Risk: retry-hint leakage could be replayed across tenants. Mitigation: advice bundles are signed and bound to tenant and route; lease tokens are single-use and TTL-limited. - Risk: older clients misinterpret new frames. Mitigation: handshake optional and negotiates a safe subset; server fallbacks to legacy behavior for unrecognized frames.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4203: add observability metrics for advice-usage and lease-token redemption. - ENG-4121: SDKs will surface structured retry decisions in the next minor release with examples for function/tool authors.

Related work: references to earlier rate-limit/idempotency efforts (see ENG-1937 retrospective) and SUP-998 customer incident (example replay causing duplicate tool side-effects).

Camila Ortega: Added key-rotation notes to docs and implemented key ID in the bundle header so we can roll keys without breaking decoders.
Ava Chen: Requested clarifications on lease token semantics: single-use vs replayable. Suggested adding explicit redemption audit events.
Camila Ortega: Lease tokens are single-use by design; added audit event emission and a unit test that verifies duplicate redemption is rejected.
Jonah Kim: Noted a flake in the e2e that surfaced under high concurrency; suggested a small backoff on client-side handshake attempts to reduce thundering herd on restart.

release_notes:
- Add optional streaming handshake to advertise server features and conservative fallbacks for older clients.
- Introduce X-Redwood-Retry machine-readable retry advice bundle (proto v1).
- Implement idempotency lease tokens for safe in-flight TTL extensions (feature-flagged).
- SDK helpers (Python/TS) to decode retry-hints and surface lease tokens to application code.
